copy_pick.why: Candidate 2 avoids the near-verbatim echo of yesterday's 'Trump waived the sanctions Congress just passed' line that sinks 1 and 3, wears the wildlife framing with its 'neighbouring pride' headline, and adds the sharpest wit with the mined-strait irony and the Butlerian Jihad aside.

doom.driver: Egypt’s Sisi seeks authorisation for defence assistance to Saudi Arabia. Egyptian president pledges 'any measure' to help defend Saudi Arabia 'if it is requested of us'.
doom.blurb: A NEIGHBOURING PRIDE PREPARES TO JOIN THE FIGHT
doom.summary: When Cairo starts asking parliament for permission to defend Riyadh, the Gulf standoff is no longer a two-player game. Meanwhile Washington and Tehran both swear they own the Strait of Hormuz, which is awkward given that naval mines keep holing ships there. Russia marked Trump's pause on its sanctions by killing eight Ukrainian civilians, and DeepSeek dropped another model while Hacker News reread the Butlerian Jihad wiki for tips.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash is out on Hugging Face and OpenRouter, keeping open-weight capability moving fast while websites start barricading against roaming AI agents.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Newsom's executive order exploring AI kill switches is a real step, but it sits beside Trump waiving the Graham Act's Russia sanctions and encryption getting squeezed from Canada to Australia.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Mined ships in Hormuz, rival US and Iranian claims of control, Egypt lining up behind Saudi Arabia, and fresh deadly Russian strikes on Ukraine add up to a multi-front war map.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: No new rogue-model incident today, but fake Claude downloads spreading malware and websites shutting out agents show the trust layer around AI is already fraying.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: France's cost-of-living protests are spreading as the yellow vests join, West Bank settler attacks are escalating after an olive-seizure edict, and a 1960 doomsday forecast quietly comes due next month.

dawn.driver: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope exceeds expectations by nearly 30%. NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has exceeded expectations after engineers made incredibly tiny adjustments to sharpen its view of the universe.
dawn.blurb: ROMAN BLOWS PAST ITS SCOUTING REPORT
dawn.summary: Engineers nudged a mirror just one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, and NASA's Roman Space Telescope now performs nearly 30% better than anyone projected, with its instruments in near-perfect alignment and ready to map the universe more sharply than planned. Down here, Stanford unveiled a label-free microscope that watches living cells work in real time. Researchers also reported a candidate drug that reversed severe fatty liver disease in animal models by restoring gut health.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Roman's Wide Field Instrument is outperforming expectations by nearly 30% after a hair-fine mirror adjustment, and Stanford's new microscope lets scientists see living cells without dyes.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: SpaceX delivered tiny brain models, 3D heart tissue and artificial-retina technology to the International Space Station, where researchers will run experiments aimed at restoring eyesight and treating brain diseases.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Pope Leo XIV left Rome's Gemelli Polyclinic fit and on his feet, and he will give the traditional Angelus blessing in St Peter's Square on Sunday.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Scientists found that the European nightjar generates thrust on its upward wingbeat, a clever trick of nature that could inspire new flying machines.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A rare pink French royal diamond, famously recovered hidden inside an apple a century ago, is going on public display for the first time.
